title: Packages contribute PWA config through powerhouse.manifest.json, and the array fields merge additively so a later layer can never drop them
content:
## A package can ship its own offline story

A package declares PWA defaults in the `powerhouse.manifest.json` it publishes, using the same shape as `connect.pwa`, so installing it works offline out of the box:

```json
{ "name": "@acme/todos",
  "pwa": { "runtimeCaching": [
    { "urlPattern": { "source": "^https://api\\.acme\\.io/" }, "handler": "NetworkFirst" } ] } }
```

The build collects fragments from the project's own root manifest, from bundled packages (`provider: "local"`, read from `node_modules`), and from non-bundled packages (`registry`, `npm`, `github`, or omitted) fetched from the registry CDN using the same version-pinned spec Connect loads at runtime. An unreachable registry is not fatal: the build warns, skips the fragment, and succeeds. A malformed fragment is likewise warned about (naming package and field) and skipped.

## The merge rule is the design decision

Precedence runs `Connect defaults < package fragments (declared order) < the project's own manifest < project connect.pwa`, with per-field-type strategies:

| Field type | Strategy |
| --- | --- |
| Manifest scalars, incl. `launch_handler` | Deep-merge — **project wins** |
| `icons`, `file_handlers`, derived `categories`, globs, `runtimeCaching`, denylist | **Additive** |
| `maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes` | The **max** across layers |

Additive arrays are the point: a package can always *add* offline coverage, and no later layer can quietly remove it. When two packages set the same scalar differently and the project does not settle it, the build warns and last-loaded wins — pin it in `connect.pwa` to decide explicitly.

`file_handlers` hands the OS a launch, so it is constrained: a fragment declares only *what* it accepts, never *where* it opens (a fragment setting its own `action` fails validation), extensions must start with a dot, and contributed entries are appended after Connect's built-in `.phd`/`.phdm` handler — browsers give each extension to the first claimant, so a package cannot hijack the built-in association.

Packages installed **at runtime** are not baked into the worker but are not ignored either: the worker serves the web-app manifest dynamically and merges their fragments in. Two extra guardrails apply there, since the end user rather than the deployer chose them — `start_url` and `scope` stay Connect's, and built-in handlers stay first.

_Source: `apps/academy/docs/academy/03-Build/05-Launch/06-ConfigurePWA.md`, Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: Precedence is Connect defaults < package fragments < project manifest < project connect.pwa. Scalars deep-merge project-wins; icons, handlers, globs and caching rules append.
